headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure between Gemini CLI and Roo Code.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and both use MCP; Gemini CLI shares state via filesystem and git, while Roo Code shares via filesystem. That creates a default path for one agent to ingest the other’s outputs as trusted content. No direct clipboard bridge is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF either agent reads instructions from shared workspace files without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through a shared MCP server or shared repo files, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable shared MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
Require provenance tags on inter-agent files.
Review any file both agents can edit before execution.
requires-engineering: add isolation or locking around shared filesystem paths.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment; Roo Code touches workspace files and browser screenshots. Because both can read/write shared filesystem content and both have broad network egress, sensitive code or secrets can flow from one agent’s workspace into the other’s outputs or model calls in default setups.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, either agent can expose them through its model/API calls.
IF browser screenshots or shell environment data are written into shared files, the other agent can read them.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Turn off network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks.
Redact screenshots and logs before saving.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, and git-state modification. Gemini CLI explicitly shares state via filesystem and git, while Roo Code shares via filesystem. Concurrent edits to the same repo can corrupt git state or overwrite each other without locking, which matches the high-risk overlap indicator.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, write conflicts can occur.
IF either agent auto-formats or rewrites files while the other is editing, state corruption is likely.
mitigations: Assign one agent per repo checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees or separate branches.
Commit frequently to reduce overlap.
requires-engineering: add file and git locks in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Both agents can act on files and shell commands, so one agent’s output can become the other’s input without a verification boundary. Gemini CLI’s MCP/tooling and Roo Code’s multi-mode workflow make it plausible that generated instructions or code are treated as authoritative, but the profiles do not show fully autonomous downstream actions, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF one agent copies the other’s generated commands into shell execution, errors can cascade.
IF either agent treats the other’s output as verified facts, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Add a verification step for generated commands.
Keep one agent in read-only mode during analysis.
Use separate task boundaries for drafting and acting.
requires-engineering: implement output provenance and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch, and both are open-source coding agents. The only compliance-relevant difference is that Roo Code can capture browser screenshots while Gemini CLI handles shell environment and files, but the pairwise compliance breach is not evidenced here, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into browser screenshots or shared files, compliance review is needed.
IF one deployment has stricter retention than the other, stored artifacts may diverge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workspaces.
Disable screenshot capture for sensitive tasks.
Align retention settings before use.
Document which agent handles which data class.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
